subject: computer-science
source_note: Topic structure follows the Pearson Edexcel GCSE Computer Science specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Data
units.blurb: Binary, data representation, storage and compression

units.name: Issues and impact
units.blurb: Environmental, ethical, legal and cybersecurity issues

units.name: Problem solving with programming
units.blurb: Designing, writing, testing and refining programs in Python

topics.name: Decomposition and abstraction
topics.blurb: Breaking problems down and modelling the real world; benefits of subprograms

topics.name: Algorithms
topics.blurb: Following and writing algorithms, trace tables, error types and standard sort/search algorithms

topics.name: Truth tables
topics.blurb: Applying AND, OR and NOT in truth tables with up to three inputs

topics.name: Binary
topics.blurb: Representing numbers in binary, two's complement, shifts, overflow and hexadecimal

topics.name: Data representation
topics.blurb: Encoding characters with ASCII and representing images and sound in binary

topics.name: Data storage and compression
topics.blurb: Binary storage units, file-size calculations and lossless/lossy compression

topics.name: Hardware
topics.blurb: Von Neumann architecture, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, memory, storage and embedded systems

topics.name: Software
topics.blurb: Operating systems, utility software and developing robust software

topics.name: Programming languages
topics.blurb: Low- and high-level languages, and how compilers differ from interpreters

topics.name: Networks
topics.blurb: Network types, internet structure, connectivity, protocols, the TCP/IP model and topologies

topics.name: Network security
topics.blurb: Identifying network vulnerabilities and methods of protecting networks

topics.name: Environmental
topics.blurb: Environmental issues from energy use, manufacture, replacement cycles and disposal

topics.name: Ethical and legal
topics.blurb: Personal data, AI and robotics issues, and intellectual property protection

topics.name: Cybersecurity
topics.blurb: Malware threats, social engineering and methods of protecting systems and data

topics.name: Develop code
topics.blurb: Decomposition, reading and refining code, converting algorithms, readability and debugging

topics.name: Constructs
topics.blurb: Structural program components and using sequence, selection, repetition and iteration

topics.name: Data types and structures
topics.blurb: Primitive and structured data types, variables, constants and string manipulation

topics.name: Input/output
topics.blurb: User input, reading/writing CSV files, validation and authentication

topics.name: Operators
topics.blurb: Using arithmetic, relational and logical operators in programs

topics.name: Subprograms
topics.blurb: Built-in and user-defined functions and procedures, parameters and variable scope

connections.why: Decomposition breaks a problem into the steps an algorithm then expresses
Logical operators used in algorithm conditions are evaluated systematically with truth tables
Programs are written by converting flowcharts and pseudocode algorithms into code
The arithmetic, relational and logical operators in algorithms are implemented directly in programs
Decomposition motivates breaking a program into reusable subprograms
All characters, images and sound are ultimately encoded using the binary number system
Storage units and file-size calculations are built on counting bits and bytes
The CPU and memory physically store and process the binary patterns data is encoded in
The operating system manages and runs on the hardware's memory, processor and devices
Translators turn high-level code into the machine code the processor and OS execute
Programs are written in a high-level language and run via a compiler or interpreter
Networking connects the hardware and devices that make up computer systems
Connecting computers in a network creates the vulnerabilities security aims to protect
File size, transmission rate and time share the same bit-based calculations
Network protection methods are part of defending digital systems against attack
Networked collection of personal data raises the privacy, ownership and consent issues examined here
Manufacturing, replacing and disposing of hardware drive environmental impacts
Constructs operate on the primitive and structured data types they manipulate
Sequence, selection and iteration are organised into reusable subprograms
Validation and file handling read and check data of the program's defined data types
Relational and logical operators form the conditions that drive selection and repetition
Robust programs validate and authenticate the input they accept from users and files
